gate_results.notes: Authoritative PlayMode run at validated commit 10245c7eb11670ea6bda283ab03e860cf52aea85 through run_unity_tests_clean.ps1, filter NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Tests.DoorLockDurabilityPlayModeTests: 13 tests, 13 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, runner exit 0, final line VALIDATION PASSED. Counts read from test-results.xml (total="13" passed="13" failed="0" skipped="0"), not the console summary. The bound manifest records commit and post_commit both 10245c7eb11670ea6bda283ab03e860cf52aea85 and tree and post_tree both e7839c381d15064033dbcc70c015a3cde99b15ae, clean before and after. All 13 cases declare NoSafeCircle.DoorPrototype.Tests.DoorLockDurabilityPlayModeTests (non-partial). The dedicated case DoorLockDurabilityFlow_MatchesFullBreachGate (its own file comment explicitly marks it VAL-001) proves the gate's full sequential narrative in one run: TakeDamage(10) on the still-sealed door leaves CurrentDurability at MaxDurability (damage before the door ever locks is rejected); OpenDoor()+CrossForward() then asserts IsLocked true and doorwayBlocker.enabled true (automatic locking and backward-player blocking); four TakeDamage(MaxDurability/4) calls break the door (IsBroken true); a further TakeDamage(10) leaves CurrentDurability at 0 (further damage calls rejected); and doorwayBlocker.enabled stays true throughout, including after the broken doorway is targeted again (player still cannot move backward). The other 12 cases in the same XML (TakeDamage_WhileSealed_IsRejected, TakeDamage_WhileOpenButNotLocked_IsRejected, ForwardCrossing_AutomaticallyLocksDoor_WithoutSecondInput, TakeDamage_WhileLocked_ReducesDurability, TakeDamage_ReducingDurabilityToZero_BreaksDoor, TakeDamage_AfterBroken_IsRejected, BrokenDoor_RemainsBroken_AndBlockerContinuesPreventingBackwardTravel, plus ForwardCrossing_RestoresPlayerHealth_ThroughOwnerControlledRestore, StartInteraction_AfterLocked_DoesNotReopenDoor, ResetDoor_RestoresLockBrokenAndDurabilityState, MaxDurability_IsPerDoorConfigurable_AndCurrentDurabilityFollowsIt) isolate each of the same clauses individually and additionally regression-test AC-002/AC-003/AC-006/AC-007 (owner-controlled health restore, no-reopen-after-lock, full reset, and per-door-configurable max durability) that VAL-001 does not itself name.

ForwardCrossing_ClosesAndLocksVisibly_AndMakesForwardProgressFinal (its own file comment explicitly marks it VAL-002) opens the test door, asserts doorwayBlocker.enabled is false beforehand (proving the door genuinely started open), then triggers only the forward-crossing trigger (CrossForward(), a single call, no second input) and asserts IsLocked true, doorVisual.activeSelf true (visibly closed) and doorwayBlocker.enabled true (locked) as the direct and only consequence -- proving 'forward-side crossing visibly closes and locks the door without a second input.' It then calls door.StartInteraction() (a literal second input attempt) and asserts IsInteracting stays false, proving the resulting blocker makes forward progress final: the door cannot be reopened afterward. Counts read from the same test-results.xml as VAL-001 (total=13 passed=13 failed=0 skipped=0).
